KP 1. Determining the Units of a Derivative
1.?

A student's parents promise to reward her R(p) dollars if she obtains an average of p points in her exams. What are the units of dRdp?

E
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 2:57 PM|Elapsed: 0:10Correct

We have that the student's reward R(p) is measured in dollars and the average exam result is measured in points. R(p):dollarsp:points

The derivative dRdp measures a change in R(p) over a change in p. So, it represents a ratio of the units: dRdp:dollarspoints

In other words, dRdp is measured in "dollars per point".

2.?

A website receives v(h) visits every h hours. What are the units of dvdh?

E
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 2:57 PM|Elapsed: 0:14Correct

We have that the time h is measured in hours and the number of visits is measured in visitors. h:hoursv(h):visitors

The derivative dvdh measures a change in v over a change in h. So, it represents a ratio of the units: dvdh:visitorshours

In other words, dvdh is measured in "visitors per hour ".

KP 2. Interpreting the Derivative of a Function
3.?

Consider a regular pentagon such that its perimeter p can vary. What is the best interpretation of p′(l) if l is the length of each diagonal of the regular pentagon?

H
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 2:58 PM|Elapsed: 0:55Correct

The function p(l) gives the perimeter of a regular pentagon with diagonal l. So,

p′(l)=dpdl=Change in pChange in l.

Therefore, p′(l) is the rate at which the perimeter changes as the diagonal changes.

4.?

Consider an equilateral triangle such that its perimeter p can vary. What is the best interpretation of A′(p) if A is the area of the triangle?

H
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 2:59 PM|Elapsed: 0:44Correct

The function A(p) gives the area of an equilateral triangle with perimeter p. So,

A′(p)=dAdp=Change in AChange in p.

Therefore, A′(p) is the rate at which the area changes as the perimeter changes.

KP 3. Interpreting the Derivative of a Function in a Given Context
5.?

The function B(T) models the number of bicycles per day, in thousands, booked at a rental service in Paris as a function of the air temperature T, measured in degrees Celsius. What is the best interpretation of the statement below?

The slope of the tangent line to the graph of B(T) at T=5 is equal to 0.4.

M
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 3:05 PM|Elapsed: 1:51Correct

The slope of the line tangent to the graph of B(T) at T=5 gives the derivative of B(T) at T=5. So, we have that

B′(5)=0.4.

We can interpret the above statement as

At a temperature of 5∘C, the number of bookings per day increases at a rate of 400 bicycles per degree of Celsius

6.?

The function B(t) gives a school's budget, in dollars, t years after the school opened. What is the best interpretation of B′(5)=−10000?

H
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 3:06 PM|Elapsed: 1:23Correct

The function B′(t) represents the rate at which the budget is changing t years after the school first opened.

Therefore, since it is negative, B′(5)=−10000 means:

5 years after opening, the school's budget decreased at a rate of 10000 dollars per year.

KP 4. Determining a Rate of Change
7.?

After taking a pill containing 300 milligrams of a particular drug, the quantity of the drug in a patient's body decreases at a rate of c(t)=300⋅2−0.7t milligrams per hour, where t is the time, in hours, since the patient consumed the pill. What will be the rate of decrease after 5 hours? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

E
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 3:08 PM|Elapsed: 1:05Correct

Since we want to determine the rate of decrease in the quantity of the drug in the patient's body after 5 hours, we have t=5.

Thus, the rate of decrease in the quantity of the drug after 5 hours will be c(5)=300⋅2−0.7(5)=300⋅2−3.5≈27.

Therefore, the rate of decrease will be 27 milligrams per hour.

8.?

The birth rate of a krill population is modeled by B(t)=5⋅20.7t thousands of tons per year, where t is the time, in years, since 1998. What was the birth rate, in thousands of tons per year, for the krill in 2008?

E
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 3:09 PM|Elapsed: 0:47Correct

The function B(t) models the birth rate for the krill, in thousands of tons, t years since 1998. Since we want the birth rate in 2008, then t=10 years.

Thus, the birth rate for the krill in 2008 was B(10)=5⋅20.7(10)=5⋅27=640.

Therefore, the birth rate for the krill in 2008 was 640 thousand tons per year.

KP 5. Relating a Derivative to a Rate of Change
9.?

Ramin, a bricklayer, is monitoring the construction of a wall by recording the following two numbers for different values of t, where t is the time, in hours, since he started his observations:

  • B(t) - the number of bricks in the wall.

  • r(t) - the rate at which the number of bricks in the wall is increasing.

What is the relationship between B(t) and r(t)?

E
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 3:31 PM|Elapsed: 7:57Correct

The function B(t) gives the number of bricks inside the wall after t hours. Then, B′(t)=dB(t)dt=Change in BChange in t.

Thus, B′(t) gives the rate at which the number of bricks increases at time t, which is the same as r(t). Therefore, the relationship between B(t) and r(t) is B′(t)=r(t).

10.?

Joseph is measuring the height reached by his lime tree by recording the following two numbers for different values of t, where t is the time, in years, since he planted the tree:

  • H(t) - The tree's height, in centimeters

  • r(t) - the rate at which the tree's height is increasing.

What is the relationship between H(t) and r(t)?

E
Wed, Jul 22nd @ 3:32 PM|Elapsed: 0:21Correct

The function H(t) gives the tree's height after t years. Then, H′(t)=dH(t)dt=Change in HChange in t.

Thus, H′(t) gives the rate at which the height of the tree increases at time t, which is the same as r(t). Therefore, the relationship between H(t) and r(t) is H′(t)=r(t).
